new_statements.quote: Tonologie La langue atteste deux tons de base (haut et bas); mais elle est déplacée dans beaucoup de mots et flottante dans plusieurs contextes.
new_statements.translation: Tonology. The language attests two basic tones (high and low); but it [tone] is displaced in many words and floating in several contexts.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lobala is described as a two-tone (H/L) language with tone shift and floating tones; the sketch says nothing about word stress or accent, and no other opened source (Morgan 1993) mentions stress either.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone described as displaced in many words and floating in several contexts; the book's introduction warns that tone marking is uncertain and often depends on position in the sentence.
new_statements.domain_note: Sketch based on questionnaire data from one speaker from Mbombe (Lobala-Sud); tone statement is about the word/lexical level with sentence-level effects noted elsewhere in the book.
new_statements.identity_note: Motingea 1990 describes the Lobala of Mbombe, i.e. Lobala-Sud (Glottolog dialect sout2817 'South Lobala'), from one speaker; Morgan 1993 worked in Imese (Kungu zone) without naming a dialect. Glottolog lists Poko [poko1262], South Lobala [sout2817] and Tanda [tand1252] as dialects; Wikipedia adds Likoka. Note that Morgan 1993 fn. 2 discusses Guthrie C.16 vs Bastin C.31j double listing and finds no evidence for two Lobala languages.

sources.quote: Tonologie La langue atteste deux tons de base (haut et bas); mais elle est déplacée dans beaucoup de mots et flottante dans plusieurs contextes.
sources.note: Section I. Phonologie (pp. 89-91) covers vowels, consonants, vowel phenomena and a one-sentence 'Tonologie' (p. 90-91): the language has two basic tones, high and low, displaced in many words and floating in several contexts. Nothing on stress/accent. Book introduction (pp. 11-12) notes that tone marking is uncertain ('T') and that tonal behaviour in many of these Ngiri varieties depends on position in the sentence; data from a questionnaire with one speaker from Mbombe (Lobala-Sud).

sources.citation: Morgan, David (1993). Vowel harmony, syllable structure, and the causative extension in Lobala: a government phonology account. Journal of West African Languages 23(1): 41-63.
sources.note: Government-phonology treatment of vowel harmony and the causative only; data are not tone-marked and the article contains no statement on Lobala tone or stress ('stress assignment' appears once as a general remark on the theory, p. 44). Fn. 2 (p. 41): 'No previous study has been made of the phonology of the Lobala language.' Image-only scan; scanned text .
